instructions: Pat the 1.5 lbs of peeled and deveined shrimp dry with paper towels. Season them with 1/2 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Slice the garlic thinly. Chop 1/4 cup of parsley. Cut the lemon in half, squeeze 1 tbsp of juice from one half into a small bowl, and cut the other half into wedges.

Put a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat and add the oil and garlic. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold and smells fragrant. Don't let it brown. Transfer the garlic to a small bowl, leaving the oil in the pan.

Turn the heat up to medium-high. Add half of the shrimp in a single layer and cook for 1 1/2 minutes per side, until pink and curled into a loose C. Transfer them to a plate and cook the other half the same way.
Pour the wine into the empty pan and scrape up the browned bits. Let it bubble for 1 minute, until it's reduced by half.
Return the shrimp and the garlic to the pan with the lemon juice and toss for 30 seconds. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the parsley.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more of the remaining 1/2 tsp of salt.
Serve with the lemon wedges. Put the red pepper flakes on the table for the adults.
method_notes: No gamberi aglio e olio page with a real number of ratings turned up: GialloZafferano's garlic and chili shrimp (unrated) cooks shrimp 3 to 4 minutes a side in garlic and olive oil, Cookpad's Gamberi Aglio, Olio e Peperoncino fries the garlic first, then the chili, then the shrimp, and CDKitchen's Gamberi con Aglio finishes with lemon, white wine and parsley. This follows GialloZafferano for the oil-and-garlic base and shrimp timing, with CDKitchen's wine and lemon for a small pan sauce, and the chili moved to the table. RecipeTin Eats' Garlic Prawns is a butter-and-garlic dish, not this one, so it is not the lead. There's no pasta, so it stays gluten-free.
